SMTO-GIT-0004 — SMTO couldn't find the Git project for this folder

GUID: e52a382f-37e2-413b-a023-09b90eba318b
Slug: git-discovery-limit
Domain: GIT · Subsystem: git

What happened

  • The folder used for a Git command is nested very deep, and SMTO stopped searching upward before it found the project. The command's own result wasn't changed; SMTO just won't remember this project.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to run the Git command directly in the project's top folder, the one that contains the hidden .git folder. Starting at the top folder means SMTO doesn't have to search through dozens of parent folders.
  2. If you aren't sure the folder is part of a Git project, ask SMTO to run git rev-parse --show-toplevel in it. If Git can't find a project either, the folder simply isn't under Git and there is nothing for SMTO to remember.
  3. If the message comes back, open Technical details in this panel and select Copy error details. The details show which folder SMTO started searching from.

What success looks like

  • A Git command run in the project's top folder finishes without this message.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details and the folder's path to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't ask them to raise SMTO's search limit; naming the project's top folder is the supported fix.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway Git discovery checked 64 parent directories above the command's working directory without finding a .git entry or a bare repository.

What this means

  • The repository search consumes all 64 parent-traversal iterations without finding a supported repository marker. These checks validate repository identity/observation. Failure of an optional observation does not establish failure or rollback of the Git command whose receipt carries it; no diagnostic rewrites Git metadata.

Why this can happen

  • The repository search consumes all 64 parent-traversal iterations without finding a supported repository marker.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the starting directory and choose the known repository root directly.

How to fix it

  • gateway_core/git_context.repository stops after 64 ancestor checks by design. Run the Git command with the repository root as its working directory (or a single git -C path to the root) so discovery starts there; do not widen the traversal bound. The observation failure does not change the Git command's result.
  • Select the repository directory directly instead of expanding the parent-search safety limit.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Exact discovery from the intended root succeeds without widening traversal bounds.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • These checks validate repository identity/observation. Failure of an optional observation does not establish failure or rollback of the Git command whose receipt carries it; no diagnostic rewrites Git metadata.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
